title: Verifying Candidate Identification Formulas over Binary Nested Markov Models
banked_reason: D0.5.G tier=subfield < floor=field; paper_score_ceiling 6.5 < 7.4, not salvageable within scope.
gap_reasons: The note proves a randomized equality test for accepted, positivity-certified binary circuits against an externally identified reference; it does not deliver a deterministic semantic decision procedure for arbitrary candidate formulas.

Its runtime bound charges the complete serialization, and marginal expansion can make that input exponential even at district width one, so the result does not establish width-only tractability for raw ID output.
The Verma proposition separates the displayed formulas algebraically, but the FID replay remains open, so an implementation failure is not established.
The absence of a runnable verifier and scaling evidence limits the projected econometrics-paper score despite the proved full-model guarantee.
proof_attempt_summary: The run proved a sound one-sided randomized polynomial-identity test for accepted, positivity-certified binary circuits, including explicit modular error accounting, a costed scalar compiler, and an algebraic four-node Verma separator. It repaired the ancestor-set proof and all cited-source dependencies, after which both D0.5 panels passed. The field claim collapsed because deterministic arbitrary-formula verification and width-only tractability were not obtained; a runnable FID replay, implementation, and scaling evidence also remain open.
tldr: A deterministic preflight checks finite rational circuits and positive-division certificates, and a width-sensitive randomized identity test compares accepted expressions on every strictly positive binary nested-Markov law of a reference graph. A mismatch returns a compact positive finite-latent causal SCM. An external reference identifier makes the result a verifier for candidate formulas over all strictly positive binary nonparametric causal DAG models with that latent projection. Every finite binary Appendix-B admissible observational formula can be compiled entrywise with expanded marginals or validated, fully charged inference circuits; successful canonical ID output is a special case. Full-query comparisons use an entrywise error allocation. Continuous variables, none-valued formulas, undefined boundary evaluations, and uncharged expanded output are outside this result.
gap: Existing selected-family formula verification and FID canonicalization do not establish the proposed full positive binary nested-model equality test with a finite certified input contract and causal mismatch witness. The rational sampling set requires a separate real open chart and a proved closure transfer.
fill: Specify and check the complete serialization; prove the support inclusion, exact latent/nested Zariski-closure adaptation, real-chart/rational-grid density chain, and modular degree-height-prime-error recurrences; then investigate costed canonical ID compilation and the Verma replay.
